title: git_sync.sh pull skipped: working tree dirty
observed: git_sync.sh $R pull printed 'pull skipped: working tree dirty — commit first (runner batches?)'; git status --short showed only ' M state/next-step.json', written by the next_step.py RESUME call itself
expected: RESUME's pull runs; a state file the RESUME call itself rewrote should not block it
hypothesis: git_sync.sh tests the whole tree for dirt; state/next-step.json is regenerated by every next_step.py invocation, so RESUME's own read makes the tree dirty before the pull

title: K1 cheat sheet: lq/sq is not produced by a 16-byte struct copy
observed: K1 §8 row: 'lq/sq $r, off($p) | 128-bit copy (u128, a 16-byte struct copy)'. Probe with mwcps2-2.4-001213 -O4,p -lang c: 'typedef struct Q { unsigned int w[4]; } Q; void copyA(Q *d, Q *s){ d[0]=s[0]; d[1]=s[1]; }' compiles to 8x lwc1 + 8x swc1, no lq/sq; a 0x40-byte struct of those compiles to an 8-byte lw/sw loop. 'typedef __int128 q128; void f(q128 *d, q128 *s){ d[0]=s[0]; }' compiles to 'lq v1,0(a1); jr ra; sq v1,0(a0)'. Spellings accepted: __int128, unsigned __int128; rejected: long128, u_long128, __uint128_t
expected: the cheat sheet names the C construct that actually produces lq/sq, so an attempt.c for an lq/sq function is written right the first time
hypothesis: mwccps2 emits lq/sq only for types whose alignment it knows to be 16, which a struct of ints does not have; the K1 row was written from reading target asm rather than from a probe compile
repro: wibo mwccps2.exe -c -O4,p -lang c probe.c; objdump -d -m mips:5900

title: calibrate: target.s includes macro.inc, which only S3 writes
observed: calibrate_compiler.py:219 emits '.include "macro.inc"' and 'glabel <fn>' into calibration/<fn>/target.s; include/macro.inc is written by gen_splat_yaml.py:215, which runs in S3 split-baseline, one step after S2. On a fresh target (stretch-panic-usa, include/ empty) all 8 cells failed at 'target assembly failed ... can't open macro.inc for reading' + 'unrecognized opcode glabel'; 0 rows reached objdiff
expected: S2 assembles its own target.s without an artifact from a later step
hypothesis: the script was written against fate-unlimited-codes-jp, whose include/macro.inc already existed from S3 when S2 was re-run; the S2-before-S3 ordering was never exercised on a fresh repo

title: calibrate: failed target assembly leaves a 0-byte target.o that the resume then trusts
observed: After F-3 the assembler had written 8 zero-byte calibration/<fn>/target.o files. calibrate_compiler.py:342 guards reassembly with 'if not tgt_o.is_file()', so the next run skipped assembly and scored against the empty files: all 168 cells recorded score=null with objdiff_error 'Loading .../target.o ... Could not read file magic', and the sweep still reported '168/168 cells done' (exit 0)
expected: a failed assembly leaves no target.o, or the guard tests for a non-empty/valid object; a sweep in which no cell could be scored does not report done
hypothesis: assemble_s lets the assembler create the output file before it errors, and the is_file() guard plus the (function, compiler, flags, c_sha256) done-key make the poisoned state sticky across runs

title: calibrate --rescore runs before targets are assembled and does not recompute bytes_equal
observed: The --rescore block is calibrate_compiler.py:311-328, the 'assemble targets once' loop is :338-346. With target.o absent, --rescore reported 'rescored 168 cell(s)' and every cell kept score=null with objdiff_error 'No such file or directory (os error 2)'; target.o (880 bytes) was assembled immediately afterwards in the same invocation. The rescore block also writes only r['score'], leaving bytes_equal=false and target_size=null from the poisoned pass — the two fields 'pin' counts
expected: --rescore assembles missing targets first and recomputes bytes_equal/target_size, so a rescored cell is as trustworthy as a freshly swept one
hypothesis: --rescore was written as a cheap objdiff-only repair for cells whose objdiff invocation failed, not for cells whose target object was itself bad
